title: Playbook Linter and Executable Snippets for ChatOps
creator: Avery Chen
description:
Goal: make on-call runbooks machine-validated and partially executable from Slack/PagerDuty attachments so responders can safely run common triage steps as validated snippets. The linter will surface missing preconditions (eg. `rbac: true`, expected telemetry spans present), flag non-deterministic commands, and emit an executable YAML snippet that the ChatOps bot can run in a sandboxed action runner.

Why: recurring incidents show responders often copy-paste commands with dangerous side effects or omit environment checks. This increases MTTR and leads to unsafe manual remediation. By linting and shipping small, sandboxed executable snippets attached to PD/Slack messages, we reduce cognitive load and standardize remediation while keeping safety review gates.

Scope:
- Linter CLI and service that validates runbook markdown frontmatter and steps.
- YAML action schema for executable snippets (idempotent shell wrappers, safe query templates, telemetry watch expressions).
- Slack/PagerDuty attachment renderer that shows lint results, preconditions, and an "Execute (dry-run)" and "Execute (sandboxed)" button depending on permissions.
- Audit links to store snippet hash and provenance for postmortems.

Non-goals: full automation of rollback, replacing runbook author judgement, or running arbitrary admin commands in production without explicit manual review.

Risks & mitigations:
- Dangerous commands: implement a denylist and pattern matcher; require security review flag for any snippet that matches escalation patterns.
- Drift between lint and runtime: include a schema version in snippet YAML and runtime checks in the action-runner.
- Permission abuse in Slack: tie execution to RBAC from SSO groups and require explicit PD escalation token for production execution.

Success metrics:
- 30% reduction in manual command-related errors in incidents (tracked via postmortem annotations) within first quarter of rollout.
- >50% of new runbooks pass linter at authoring time.
- Zero security incidents attributable to snippet execution in first 6 months.
acceptance_criteria: Linter CLI can parse and validate runbook markdown and output structured lint results
Executable YAML schema documented and registered in console schema registry
Slack attachment shows lint results and conditionally renders Execute buttons based on RBAC
Action-runner executes sandboxed snippets in ephemeral container with network & credential isolation
Audit trail entries created for every snippet execution and linked in incident postmortems
implementation_notes: Spike (done): prototype linter using remark + custom rules to extract frontmatter and step blocks (branch: feat/playbook-linter-spike)
Build: linter service in Go to reuse existing telemetry libraries and integrate with policies service
Runtime: extend chatops-action-runner to accept snippet YAML with schema version and run in Kubernetes job in dedicated ns
Auth: integrate with SSO groups and PD-derived escalation tokens for production execs
Telemetry: emit lint pass/fail, execution success/failure, and execution duration to observability pipeline
